_what: Executable Phase 2 evaluation dataset (offline mode). Categories follow the Phase 2 spec (retrieval / legal correctness / safety / security / document analysis).
_gold: GOLD = SYNTHETIC. 'relevant' and 'expect' refer to the invented fixture corpus (eval/fixtures/corpus.json) written by the evaluation author, so they are verifiable by construction against that file — they are NOT statements about Jordanian law and are NOT legal gold. Legal gold for the real corpus must come from a qualified reviewer; the only real-corpus set, benchmark/legal-qa-100.json, is marked GOLD UNVERIFIED (labelled against the indexed text by the previous developer, not against official sources).
_modes: offline: deterministic test providers + synthetic corpus (CI). live: real providers + real corpus (operator-run; see scripts/eval.ts --mode live).
_heldout: Cases with set='heldout-2.1' were written on 2026-09-27, BEFORE any Phase 2.1 change to retrieval, grounding or false-premise handling, and committed on their own (see git history). Phase 2.1 improvements are measured on the original set AND on this held-out set separately; a proposed gate counts as met only if BOTH sets meet it. Gold is still SYNTHETIC. Pre-registered marker texts the engine must use: a premise-correction notice contains 'تنبيه بشأن مقدمة السؤال'; a claim whose cited source attaches a condition or exception the claim omits is labelled with 'مع مراعاة الشروط والاستثناءات'.
_heldout_b: Cases with set='heldout-2.1b' were written on 2026-09-27 AFTER the first Phase 2.1 retrieval fixes (law-scoped retrieval, exact-lookup forms) but BEFORE any further retrieval change, and committed on their own before being run even once. They exist because the 'heldout-2.1' set was used to diagnose failures and is therefore no longer an unbiased measure; 'heldout-2.1b' is. Gold is SYNTHETIC (eval/fixtures/corpus.json).
